In this record, the essence of our family’s shared identity is beautifully preserved through a series of heartfelt interviews with our very own family members. Through these candid conversations, we explore the profound question, "What does it mean to be a member of this family?" Each interview offers a unique perspective, weaving together the threads of our collective history, values, and cherished memories. As members of the Polston family, this archive serves as a cherished testament to our bond, reminding us of our roots and the values that have shaped us. These interviews are a heartfelt gift from our ancestors to us, and together, they form a tapestry of our legacy for future generations. So, take a moment to immerse yourself in the stories and reflections shared by our kin, and let this archive strengthen the ties that bind us as one resilient and loving family.

Nurturing Spiritual Health: The Guiding Light of the Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation
metadata.description:
The core values of the Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation are deeply rooted in the histories and legacies of the Miller, Myers, and Estes families. Beyond their commitment to education and athleticism, one core value shines as a guiding light in their philanthropic journey: Spiritual Health. This profound commitment to spiritual well-being reflects the family's strong connection to their faith and their unwavering dedication to uplifting communities through their generosity.

 Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation

content.content: The journey towards spiritual health begins with the families that paved the way for Bill and Elinor Miller's philanthropic endeavors. John C. Myers, an industrialist, art collector, and philanthropist, was more than a successful businessman. He was a man deeply dedicated to his spiritual beliefs, values that would shape the trajectory of his family for generations to come. These values were mirrored in the grandeur of the Myers mansion, which would later serve as the heart of Ashland Theological Seminary. His legacy as a generous benefactor would leave an indelible mark on the community and lay the foundation for future acts of spiritual kindness.Similarly, the Miller family, with T.W. Miller at its helm, shared a profound commitment to the spiritual growth of their community. This dedication to faith and the spiritual well-being of others manifested in various forms, from their philanthropic contributions to their active participation in local institutions. These values were deeply rooted in the Miller family's industrialist and philanthropic endeavors, reflecting their belief in the transformative power of spirituality in enriching lives.Elinor and Bill Miller's devotion to spiritual growth further solidified the importance of this core value. Their unwavering support for Ashland Theological Seminary is a testament to their commitment to nurturing spiritual health within their community. The seminary's location on the expansive Myers-Miller property, made available through the generosity of both families, symbolizes the convergence of faith, philanthropy, and community development.The Myers mansion, where administrative and faculty offices are housed, stands as a reminder of John C. Myers' dedication to spirituality and philanthropy. It is not merely a building but a sanctuary where individuals can explore their faith, engage in meaningful discussions, and deepen their spiritual well-being. Surrounding the campus are formal gardens, a swimming pool, and a tennis court, all providing spaces for reflection and spiritual connection.Furthermore, the presence of two statues, The Divine Servant and The Fisher of Men, sculpted by Max Greiner of Texas, serves as a visual representation of the spiritual values held dear by the Miller family. These statues evoke feelings of compassion, service, and spiritual growth, embodying the foundation's commitment to nurturing these values within the community.The Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation's enduring contributions to institutions like Ashland Theological Seminary reinforce its commitment to spiritual health. By supporting centers like the Smetzer Counseling Center and creating spaces for reflection, the foundation strives to empower individuals on their spiritual journeys, fostering a sense of unity and spiritual growth.Bill and Elinor Miller's belief in the importance of spiritual health has left an indelible mark on their philanthropic legacy. Their actions and contributions reflect a deep understanding of the role spirituality plays in enriching lives and communities. Through the Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation, their dedication to spiritual well-being continues to shine as a beacon of hope and healing for generations to come.

metadata.title: Athletic Excellence: The Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation's Impact
metadata.description:
Athleticism has long been a cherished value for the Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation, deeply rooted in the legacies of Bill and Elinor Miller. Bill, affectionately known as the "Father of Ashland Fast-Pitch Softball," was born into a family with a rich history in Ashland, Ohio, and his dedication to sports played a significant role in their lives.

Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation

content.content: One of Bill's most notable contributions to athletics was his creation of the Rubbermen, a fast-pitch softball team, in 1959. Within a remarkably short period, the Rubbermen had risen to become one of the premier teams in both the state and the nation. Under the guidance of Coach Chuck Smiley, the team clinched a remarkable third-place finish in the ASA Nationals in 1966. This achievement was a testament to Bill's passion and leadership, and it marked the beginning of a storied legacy in Ashland fast-pitch softball.Yet, Bill's commitment to athletics extended far beyond the softball diamond. He was an active supporter of various local agencies and organizations, including the Ashland YMCA, Samaritan Regional Health System, Ashland University, and the Country Club of Ashland. These contributions showcased his genuine love for Ashland and its people, reflecting his belief in the power of sports to unite and uplift communities.The YMCA, in particular, held a special place in Bill's heart, echoing his family's historical ties to community development. The Myers family, known for their successful business ventures, played a pivotal role in Ashland's industrial growth. In 1905, they made a significant contribution towards the construction of the Ashland YMCA, envisioning it as a sanctuary for young men seeking a positive alternative to pool halls and taverns. Over a century later, the Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation continued this legacy, generously supporting both the Ashland, Ohio YMCA and the YMCA of Central Florida. These contributions not only honored Bill's family heritage but also reinforced the importance of community engagement and physical wellness, making athleticism a cornerstone of the foundation's values.Bill's dedication to sports was not confined to his hometown; it extended to his involvement with the Rollins College Board of Trustees. Serving as the Athletic chair, he played a vital role in shaping the university's sports programs and promoting the significance of physical fitness and sportsmanship among students. This engagement underscored his belief in the transformative power of athletics as a means of personal growth and character development.The Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation, carrying forward the vision and values of Bill and Elinor, acknowledges the profound impact of athleticism on individuals and communities. Through its generous contributions to organizations like Rollins College and Grace Medical Home, the foundation empowers individuals to pursue their athletic aspirations and lead healthier lives. Whether it's supporting youth programs, fostering senior health through arts enrichment, or promoting physical well-being, the foundation's commitment to athleticism stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of Bill and Elinor Miller. They believed in the transformative power of sports and community engagement.

metadata.title: Family Legacies: The Foundations of Bill and Elinor Miller’s Commitment
metadata.description:
T.W. Miller Jr., fondly known as Bill, and his wife Elinor, were prominent figures in their communities, driven by a deep commitment to making a positive impact. Their journey toward founding the Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation was rooted in their shared values, upbringing, and a desire to give back to society.  Today, the foundation focuses to impact the lives of those in Ashland, OH and Winter Park, FL through a commitment to community engagement, education, athleticism, spiritual health, and health care.   

Elinor & T.W. Miller Foundation

content.content:
Bill Miller

Bill Miller, the son of T.W. and Helen Miller and the grandson of F.E. Myers, emerged as a prominent and respected public figure known for his strong commitment to both business and community service. His life was marked by a dedication to enhancing the well-being of his community and alma mater, Rollins College, while also leaving an indelible mark on various institutions and organizations in Winter Park, Florida. 

Born in the heart of Ashland, Ohio, Bill's early years were influenced by his family's legacy in the rubber industry. He understood the value of hard work and responsible leadership from a young age, having witnessed his family's dedication to the Faultless Rubber Company. This upbringing instilled in him a sense of humility and an unwavering commitment to community service.Bill's educational journey took him to Rollins College in Winter Park, Florida. His time at Rollins not only provided him with a well-rounded education but also deepened his connection to the Winter Park community. His graduation from Rollins marked the beginning of his lifelong dedication to the college and the surrounding area.
